name: Dissociated and Sidon sets: Sarkozy / Szemeredi-Vu / Lev structure of subset sums, with constructive long APs (Chen-Mao-Zhang)
description: Collects the structure theory for subset sums of a set A of integers. Sarkozy's finite addition theorems (1989, 1994) and Lev's refinements say that if A inside [0,m] is dense enough (|A| about m/k or more) and gcd(A)=1 after shifting, then a bounded multiple of A (or of its subset sums) contains a full arithmetic progression of length about m. Szemeredi-Vu (JAMS 2006) extend this to long APs and proper GAPs in subset sums of dense sets; Conlon-Fox-Pham give homogeneous versions. Chen-Mao-Zhang (arXiv 2503.19299) make the Sarkozy/Lev theorems constructive: a near-linear-time algorithm returns the AP together with an explicit representation of each term as a sum of elements of A, bypassing the non-constructive Mann and Kneser theorems via a 'greedy sumset' operation and an AP-augmentation framework. Dissociated (all subset sums distinct) and Sidon-type sets are the opposite pole: no short additive structure, so they give the shape of sets with the fewest relations.
authors_year_venue: Lin Chen, Yuchen Mao, Guochuan Zhang, arXiv:2503.19299 (v3, 7 Apr 2025), cs.DS. Background: A. Sarkozy 1989/1994 (finite addition theorems); V. Lev 1997 'Finite Addition Theorem I' and 'On consecutive subset sums' (Discrete Math 1998); E. Szemeredi and V. Vu, JAMS 19 (2006) 119-169; D. Conlon, J. Fox, H. T. Pham, arXiv:2311.01416; S. Dutta, 'The greedy algorithm for dissociated sets', arXiv:2601.07068.
status_and_verification: Chen-Mao-Zhang: preprint (likely a published TCS venue version exists, not checked). Read via alphaXiv full text: abstract, introduction, statements of Theorems 1.1-1.5; proofs (greedy sumset, AP augmentation) NOT read in detail. Szemeredi-Vu, Conlon-Fox-Pham, Dutta and Sarkozy original statements were NOT read; they are known only from recall and from how Korsky (arXiv:2606.24139) and Chen (arXiv:2609.00044) cite them.
key_theorem_or_bound: [uncertain] Chen-Mao-Zhang Theorem 1.2 (constructive Finite Addition Theorem I): for A inside Z[0,m] with |A|=n, 0 in A, gcd(A)=1, and n > (m+1)/k, one can compute in O(n log m) time an AP {s}+{0,1,...,m} contained in 332k * A (k-fold sumset), together with a randomized witness. The non-constructive source is Lev 1997 Thm 1 (Finite Addition Theorem I): same hypotheses with n > (m-1)/k + 2 give {s}+{0..m} inside (2k-1)A. Theorem 1.4 gives the analogue for subset sums (Finite Addition Theorem II, Sarkozy/Lev) with an O-tilde(n)-time algorithm; application: an O-tilde(n)-time algorithm for the SEARCH version of dense Subset Sum, and for Unbounded Subset Sum with t > c a_max^2/n a solution in O(n log a_max). Exact constants and the precise form of Thm 1.3/1.4 were only partly read.
regime_exponents: Dense regime only: needs |A| >= about sqrt(m) up to m/k, i.e. m = poly(n) (or at most about n^2 for the subset-sum version). Hard instances of the repo have a_i of size 2^{Theta(n)}, so m is exponential in n and none of these hypotheses holds. No statement about beta, D* thresholds, 0.311n, 0.5n or 0.661n; n/2 baseline not touched.
proof_type_and_tools: [uncertain] Combinatorial/algorithmic. Original proofs use Mann's theorem and Kneser's theorem (non-constructive). Constructive replacement: greedy sumset (a large subset of the sumset with efficiently searchable representations) and an iterative AP-augmentation framework playing the role of Kneser. Szemeredi-Vu use Fourier/inverse-type arguments plus sumset theory.
quantitative_loss: Constant-factor loss in the multiplicity of the sumset (332k copies versus 2k-1 non-constructively); polylog factors in running time. The density threshold n > m/k is polynomial in m. Nothing here survives when m is exponential in n: the density n/m is exponentially small, far below every threshold.
worst_case_vs_average_case: Worst-case over all A in the dense regime (deterministic structure); the randomized part is only in the witness-finding step. Does not transfer to the exponentially sparse worst case needed for C1/C2.
coefficient_set: [uncertain] Sumsets kA (coefficients 0..k with repetition, i.e. multiset version) for Thm 1.2; genuine {0,1} subset sums for the Finite Addition Theorem II / Sarkozy-Lev-Szemeredi-Vu line. Dissociated sets concern {0,1} (and bounded-coefficient variants {0..q}, q-fold dissociated).
subset_size_regime: All subset sums with unrestricted size; no control of Theta(n)-size subsets (the AP terms are produced by subsets of unspecified size). Distinct-size control would require a separate argument.
relevance_to_Nc: If A inside [0,m] with m small relative to 2^n (dense), then 2^n subset sums fall in [0, nm], so heavy collisions are forced and the AP structure gives many equal-sum pairs; constructive versions would let one extract them. A dissociated set has N_c = 0, so a large N_c requires leaving the dissociated class. The relevant statement for C1 is only through the contrapositive: few relations (N_c small) forces a sparse/dissociated-like set, and that is where the hard instances live.
relevance_to_Dstar: D* is the minimum size of the weight-n/8 half-sumset T(S1,S2). Dissociation of the support gives a LOWER bound on D* (repo lemma: k-dissociated with k=2j implies D* >= C(m/4+j,j)^2). Conversely D* <= 2^{0.311n} forces short relations. Szemeredi-Vu/Sarkozy structure would say that small T(S1,S2) with dense support means GAP structure, but the dense hypothesis is not available for a support of size n/2 spread over 2^{Theta(n)}, so these results do not forbid D* <= 2^{0.311n} on their own.
applicability_gap: [uncertain] Fails for: (i) exponential magnitude (density threshold); (ii) {0,1} versus k-fold sumsets with repetition for Thm 1.2; (iii) no control of subset sizes (Theta(n) required); (iv) polynomial doubling is not assumed or available for subset-sum sets of sparse supports; (v) the AP produced has length about m, a statement about values, not about the number of relations.
counterexample_or_hard_instance_family: Dissociated/Sidon-like families (powers of 2, Conway-Guy, Bohman sets: no relations at all); box supports (m vectors in [0,L)^d with random generators) that are k-dissociated for k about d log(kL)/log(m/k) yet have D* <= (mL/2)^d (from the repo's HIGH_ENERGY.md); rank-d GAPs with random generators.
dependency_chain: Composes with: inverse_littlewood_offord (concentration forces GAP), distinct_subset_sums_extremal (how large dissociated sets must be), lattice_relation_detection (finding the relations), and with Kneser/Mann/Lev for the dense endgame; it would be the final, constructive step after a Freiman-type structure result (BSG then PFR then constructive Freiman) in a branch-or-bin argument.
constructiveness: Yes: near-linear time O(n log m) (Thm 1.2) or O-tilde(n) for dense subset sum, returning an explicit AP and per-term representations as sums of elements of A. Only in the dense regime m = poly(n).
lean_formalizable: [uncertain] Unlikely in a mathlib-free setting for the full theorems (Kneser/Mann are heavy). The easy lemma (k-dissociated implies D* >= C(m/4+j,j)^2) is already elementary and formalizable.
computational_check: [uncertain] Source reports theory and running time only; no experiments were seen. In the repo, at n <= 40 one can test dissociation exactly by counting collisions among the 2^n subset sums via sort or meet-in-the-middle (feasible up to about n=30 directly, to 40 with 2^20 half lists) and tabulate N_c and D* for dissociated/AP/GAP families in scripts/analysis.
next_experiment: Measure, for random supports of size n/2 at n = 24, 32, 40 with magnitude 2^{cn}, the smallest k for which the support stops being k-dissociated, as a function of c; compare with the repo's k(delta) threshold and with Sarkozy-type density predictions to see where AP structure first appears.
open_issues: Nothing proved for exponentially sparse sets; Chen-Mao-Zhang give no sparse-regime structure. The exact hypotheses of Thm 1.1-1.4 were extracted from a text dump and the displayed fractions (e.g. (m-1)/k + 2 versus (m+1)/k) should be rechecked against the PDF before citing.
